articles.headline: Sources: Giants QB Jaxson Dart believed to have sprained MCL
articles.description: Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart is believed to have suffered a sprained MCL on Monday night based on initial exams, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo. X-rays were negative and he will undergo an MRI on Tuesday.
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart is believed to have suffered a sprained MCL during Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo, after taking a hard hit on his left knee during his team's first series.

X-rays were negative, according to sources, and Dart will undergo an MRI on Tuesday. He is expected to miss some time. 

Dart was hurt while being pressured on third-and-8. Rams linebacker Byron Young hit Dart from the quarterback's right side, sending him into linebacker Josaiah Stewart as he tried to tackle Dart, who landed hard on the turf. 

The second-year quarterback immediately grabbed at his left knee and went to the blue medical tent, where he was examined. He came out and walked with a limp to the locker room.

The team initially said he was questionable to return because of a knee injury but announced early in the third quarter that he would not return.

"He's going to be OK," Giants general manager Joe Schoen told ESPN's Laura Rutledge at halftime.

Sources told ESPN that Dart tried to get back into the game in the first half, but the Giants wouldn't let him. He returned to the New York sideline in street clothes.

Jameis Winston replaced Dart at quarterback and went 11-of-27 for 111 yards with an interception.

Dart wasn't the only Giants star who left the game in the first half. Wide receiver Malik Nabers was hurt trying to make a catch in the second quarter.

Cornerback Trent McDuffie knocked down a pass intended for Nabers, who immediately grabbed at his right shoulder. Nabers went to the sideline and sank to the ground, where he was attended to by trainers for several minutes.

The third-year wide receiver, who came back last week from a torn ACL, then went to the bench and put a towel over his head. He was initially listed as questionable but returned to the field later in the second quarter.

The injuries didn't stop there, either.

Giants left tackle Andrew Thomas went to the medical tent in the fourth quarter with a groin injury and didn't return to the game. And linebacker Brian Burns suffered an ankle injury in the closing minutes of the game and couldn't put weight on his leg as he left the field.

Information from The Associated Press was included in this report.

articles.headline: Rams defeat depleted Giants 28-6 on 'Monday Night Football'
articles.description: L.A. exceeded expectations after its Week 1 loss, while New York saw injuries to its stars and couldn't keep up with Matthew Stafford & Co.
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- The Rams' offense struggled to get into a rhythm during the season opener, but over the week that followed, Los Angeles wide receiver Davante Adams cautioned against overreacting to that small sample size.

"Everybody's freaking out, which I understand," Adams said last week. "We didn't put together the greatest showing out there. But you're a fool if you think that that's what it's going to look like every single week."

On Monday night against the New York Giants, quarterback Matthew Stafford and Adams showed off the connection that flashed midway through last season, the wideout's first with the Rams. Adams logged eight catches for 195 yards and two touchdowns during a 28-6 win in which L.A. was without wide receiver Puka Nacua.

Adams' performance sparked a return to the offense the Rams were expecting going into the season. It was Adams' 29th career game with multiple receiving touchdowns, tied for fourth most in NFL history.

Adams' 195 yards were the most receiving yards by any player in a game so far this season, and without Nacua, second-year tight end Terrance Ferguson was the Rams' second-leading receiver. Ferguson tallied six catches for 54 yards and a touchdown. 

Here are the most important things to know for both teams:

Los Angeles Rams (1-1)

What to make of the QB performance: Stafford, who had a passer rating of 61.2 in Los Angeles' season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers, had a passer rating of 131.3 on Monday night. He completed 22 of 31 passes for 327 yards, with four touchdowns and an interception. Stafford had success passing 10 or more yards downfield, something he struggled with in Week 1. After going 3-for-10 for 74 yards with an interception on those throws in Week 1, Stafford went 9-for-13 for 219 yards in Week 2, with two touchdowns and an interception.

Trend to watch: What will Aaron Donald's workload look like going forward? On Monday night, he played 32 defensive snaps (58.2%) for the Rams. He was credited with three tackles, one run stuff and no quarterback pressures. The game was Donald's first in 981 days, as he initially retired following the 2023 season.

Stat to know: Adams' first-quarter touchdown was his first with the Rams that came on a pass not thrown into the end zone, according to ESPN Research. Each of Adams' 15 receiving touchdowns last season (14 in the regular season, one in the playoffs) was thrown into the end zone. -- Sarah Barshop

Next game: at Denver Broncos, 8:20 p.m. ET

New York Giants (1-1)

The New York Giants may have dodged disaster with injuries to star quarterback Jaxson Dart and wide receiver Malik Nabers. They still couldn't avoid a reality check in a 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams at Sofi Stadium.

articles.headline: Rams' Stafford passes Rivers for 6th all time in passing TDs
articles.description: Rams QB Matthew Stafford moved to sixth all-time in passing touchdowns after throwing his 426th to Davante Adams on Sunday night.
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford passed Philip Rivers for sole possession of sixth on the NFL's career passing touchdown list after a stellar performance in Monday night's 28-6 win over the New York Giants. 

Stafford's third-quarter 11-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Davante Adams was his 426th career regular-season touchdown, moving him past a tie with Rivers. It was also his third touchdown of the game -- he ended with four total to go along with 327 passing yards. 

Stafford now trails only Tom Brady (649), Drew Brees (571), Peyton Manning (539), Aaron Rodgers (528) and Brett Favre (508) on the all-time list.

Stafford is the second player in NFL history with 25 or more three-passing-touchdown games for multiple franchises (25 Rams, 42 Lions), according to ESPN Research. Manning had 64 with the Colts and 29 with the Broncos.

articles.headline: Davante Adams, Matthew Stafford lead Rams past Giants 28-6 after Jaxson Dart's injury
articles.description: — Davante Adams made eight catches for 195 yards and hauled in two of Matthew Stafford’s four touchdown passes, and the Los Angeles Rams welcomed Aaron Donald back...
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- — Davante Adams made eight catches for 195 yards and hauled in two of Matthew Stafford’s four touchdown passes, and the Los Angeles Rams welcomed Aaron Donald back to the NFL with a 28-6 victory over the New York Giants on Monday night.


              Stafford passed for 327 yards for the Rams (1-1), who capitalized after the Giants (1-1) lost Jaxson Dart to a left knee injury on their first offensive series.


              The Rams played without injured All-Pros Puka Nacua and Myles Garrett, but Stafford and Adams put on a vintage performance while the preseason Super Bowl favorites rebounded competently from last week’s 27-7 debacle of a loss to the 49ers in Australia.


              Adams’ catches and yards receiving were both his best performances in a Rams uniform, while league MVP Stafford moved into sixth in NFL history with his 426th career TD pass, topping Philip Rivers when Adams adroitly tracked down an 11-yard fade in the third quarter.


              Jameis Winston went 11 of 27 for 111 yards with an interception in place of Dart, who left the field shakily after taking a huge hit from Byron Young and Josaiah Stewart on New York's seventh play. The second-year quarterback, who looked great in last week's win over Dallas, watched the second half in a track suit while the Giants managed just 182 yards of offense compared to LA's 481.


              The night was also a milestone for Donald, who had three tackles for the Rams while completing his comeback with his first NFL game action in 32 months. The three-time AP NFL Defensive Player of the Year, who skipped the Week 1 trip to Melbourne, got wild cheers from Rams fans at every opportunity at SoFi Stadium.


              Adams was extraordinary in the second game of his 13th NFL season. He made a two-handed grab high above his head before taking it for a 31-yard touchdown on the Rams’ second possession, and he made a 64-yard catch on their third drive to set up Kyren Williams’ 10-yard TD catch.


              Winston and the Giants' offense couldn't get much going after Dart's exit. Winston threw an end-zone interception to Trent McDuffie in the second quarter, and New York managed only a field goal after Jevon Holland forced and recovered a fumble at the Los Angeles 11 right before halftime, with Donald stuffing Najee Harris on a classic third-down tackle.


              Stafford put it away with a TD pass to Terrance Ferguson with 8:57 to play.


              Injuries
              Giants pass rusher Brian Burns went down with a lower left leg injury in the fourth quarter. He turned down a cart ride postgame. ... WR Malik Nabers injured his shoulder and missed time in the first half, but returned. ... Rams RB Ronnie Rivers injured his calf.


              Up next
              Giants: Host Tennessee on Sunday.


              Rams: At Denver on Sunday night.


              ------

articles.headline: Who has the most home runs for each MLB team all-time?
articles.description: Check out each team's all-time home run leaders.
articles.body:
No player in MLB history has hit more home runs for a single franchise than Hank Aaron, who launched 733 for the Braves. Every team has its own home run king and, as we progress through the 2026 season, a changing of the guard occurred in Kansas City.

On July 25, Salvador Perez climbed past George Brett on the Royals' all-time home run list after blasting his 318th career homer.

Below are each team's all-time home run leaders. Players in bold are still active on their respective teams.

articles.headline: River Ryan, key piece in Tarik Skubal deal, leads Tigers
articles.description: River Ryan, acquired from the Dodgers in the Tarik Skubal trade, was outstanding in his Detroit debut Monday night, pitching three scoreless innings in a win against the Nationals.
articles.body:
DETROIT -- River Ryan was outstanding in his Detroit debut and the Tigers hit three home runs to rout the Washington Nationals 9-2 on Monday night, one day after being eliminated from the American League playoff race.

Ryan, acquired from the Los Angeles Dodgers in the Tarik Skubal trade, pitched three scoreless innings. ESPN's No. 51-ranked prospect allowed two hits and a walk with two strikeouts. Ryan is expected to start again in the season finale Sunday -- the day after Justin Verlander is scheduled to make his final major league start.

"I think with, kind of what I've been through this year with injuries and kind of being stuck behind a really elite rotation with the Dodgers, it was just great to be able to get out there and play ball at the big league level again," Ryan told reporters. 

Keider Montero (10-9) pitched four scoreless innings in relief of Ryan.

Washington starter DJ Herz (0-1) made his first big league appearance in nearly two years. Herz, who had Tommy John surgery in April 2025, pitched four innings, allowing four runs on five hits and two walks while striking out four.

The Tigers took a 2-0 lead in the first. Gleyber Torres walked, went to second on a wild pitch and scored on a ground-rule double from Hao-Yu Lee. After Herz got the first out, Eduardo Valencia singled to left field, with Lee scoring when James Wood misplayed the ball for an error.

Javier Baez made it 4-0 in the fourth, hitting his third homer of the season over the Tigers bullpen in left to bring home Dillon Dingler.

Detroit added five more runs in the fifth, three on Ben Malgeri's fourth homer and two on Spencer Torkelson's 25th.

That made it 9-0, but Yohandy Morales hit a two-run homer to get the Nationals on the scoreboard in the eighth.

The Tigers announced before the game that, due to a bank merger, Comerica Park will be known as Fifth Third Park starting in 2027. That's the same name as the stadium for the Toledo Mud Hens, Detroit's Triple-A team.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

articles.headline: Pete Alonso homers twice to reach 40 on the season, helps Orioles rally to 4-3 win over Blue Jays
articles.description: — Pete Alonso homered twice, including a two-run shot in the eighth inning that lifted the Baltimore Orioles to a 4-3 victory over the Toronto Blue Jays on Monday night.
articles.body:
BALTIMORE -- — Pete Alonso homered twice, including a two-run shot in the eighth inning that lifted the Baltimore Orioles to a 4-3 victory over the Toronto Blue Jays on Monday night.


              The Orioles are on the verge of elimination in the American League wild-card race, but Alonso has been terrific in his first season with the team. He has 40 home runs — the fourth time he's reached that mark in a season — and he's opened a nine-RBI lead on Triple Crown hopeful Yordan Alvarez of Houston.


              In fact, Alonso might be the one who ends up leading the AL in homers and RBI. He's one home run behind Tampa Bay slugger Junior Caminero.


              The Blue Jays brought in submarine right-hander Tyler Rogers (2-3) to face Alonso, who became just the second right-handed hitter to homer off him over the last two seasons.


              Yennier Cano (4-3) won in relief for the Orioles, and Rico Garcia worked a perfect ninth for his 10th save.


              Nathan Lukes and George Springer hit RBI singles during Toronto's three-run first inning, but the Blue Jays fell 3 1/2 games behind the idle Chicago White Sox for the final wild card in the AL.


              Trey Yesavage returned to the mound for the Blue Jays after knee inflammation sent him to the injured list in early August. He pitched only two innings, allowing a home run to Alonso in the first.


              Gunnar Henderson homered in the sixth for the Orioles and finished a double shy of the cycle.


              After the start was delayed 47 minutes because of rain, the first four Toronto batters reached base. Shane Baz was called for a pitch-clock violation with the count full to Brett Bateman. Then he issued another walk to Alejandro Kirk on a debatable checked-swing call.


              Lukes and Springer followed with hits to make it 2-0. A sacrifice fly by Sean Keys brought home another run.


              Baz held Toronto scoreless after that and made it through 6 2/3 innings.


              Bateman left the game with a hip injury after making a sliding catch in center field in the second. X-rays were negative.


              Up next
              Blue Jays RHP Max Scherzer (3-8) starts Tuesday night against Chris Bassitt (8-5) of the Orioles.


              ------
